answer: Behavioral correlation scoring. The system groups new identities by shared timing, language quirks, and IP ranges, then flags tight clusters that wander across the same transaction patterns. To forge a convincing cluster, an attacker must inject irregular delays and varied phrasing per account, raising cost from near zero to sustained manual effort per identity. Detection runs after the fact on a sampled dune of interaction logs, so the attacker pays for maintenance labor, not just registration.
